They did state interpretation: negative indicates improvement. That's explicit. They also noted batch B unit correction and said naive baseline vs final would be false. They mention batch-B unit problem. So they did note that issue. However they didn't specify "improved for whom". The requirement: "Genuinely under-specified: improved for whom (all patients? by arm?), and 'improved' means baseline-minus-final, where LOWER is better. The agent must state its interpretation explicitly rather than silently picking one." The analyst did state interpretation (negative indicates improvement) but they used final - baseline, not baseline - final. That's a mismatch. Also they didn't discuss "for whom".
